At least, that's what the introductory text says. None of this actually happens in the game.

Gameplay starts with character creation, where a number of useless stats are generated for the player. Regardless, the player will become a female dwarf amazon weighing 335 lb.The player starts in an invisible maze with identical rooms, and regardless what direction the player moves, they will become lost, eventually finding themselves in a desert. After wandering aimlessly, the player will encounter several defenseless enemies which are crushed without mercy.

It doesn't matter what direction the player travels, they will always encounter the same enemies, requiring them to lose combat with a lizardman, and get stomped to death by a giant chicken. The player is resurrected both times. Ultimately, the player will get slain by a zombie, and just kind of win the game.

421727.overview:
A game apparently developed by aliens, it was intercepted by the programmers at Southwestern Data Systems, whom were able to translate the game to work on Apple II computers, but were unable to convert the game text to English. In this game, the aliens are understandably depicted in the protagonist role, as they show their invasion of Earth.

In the first scene, the player controls an alien on the top of the screen, whom can move horizontally and fire vertically downwards. They player has to fire missiles at Earth shuttles and rockets which launch towards the player. The player gets points for destroying human vessel, and if a vessel manages to move past the player, the player's round is over, and they receive a score for this component. In the second game, the player can move in 4 cardinal directions, and must place landmines in the way of approaching human tanks. If the tank runs over a mine, it is destroyed. If the player runs into a tank while holding a mine, they lose a life and the tank is destroyed. The player has a total of 3 lives, and when all are lost it's game over.

421740.overview:
Break the Bank! is a blackjack teaching tool and simulator.

Designed to teach players techniques for improving their skill at blackjack, the program offers tutorials in four levels of blackjack play, from best play without card counting to advanced card counting techniques. The program contains drills and flashcards designed to improve the player's blackjack play. The player can also input their own strategies, and see how they compete against the strategies in game.

Finally, there is an actual graphical animated blackjack game, where the player competes against the computer to put their blackjack skills into practice. Game rules follow typical Las Vegas blackjack play.

421745.overview: In Brainteaser Boulevard! the player takes control of a scout whose task it is to help old ladies cross a busy street full of cars and trucks. The game is similar to Frogger (albeit without the river section), with the player starting out at the bottom of the screen and having to move from lane to lane while avoiding the vehicles that pass by. Once he has reached the top of the screen he has to go all the way back but this time accompanied by an old lady. A level is completed when there are no more ladies to save. There are two difficulties: advanced and beginner. In the former there are three ladies and fast cars while in the latter there are five ladies but the cars are slower.

421759.overview:
Bop-A-Bet is an educational typing and letter-recognition game for children.

Four letters appear on the screen, and the player must correctly choose the letters in alphabetical order. If the player correctly selects a letter, the next letter alphabetically will appear somewhere on the screen, and the correct letter will disappear. The player can select from uppercase or lowercase letter recognition, and receives 10 points for each letter correctly selected, and loses 5 points for a mistake. After reaching the letter Z, the player enters a bonus mode where they can bop punching bags for 20 points each. The player can set a time-limit per letter to increase or decrease the difficulty level.

421856.overview:
Bezoff is a series of 3 insect-themed 1-player arcade game.

The player has a series of 3 mini-games with the goal of maximizing their score during these games. To choose which order to play the games, the player starts by controlling a small circle in a hallway connected to three rooms. The player moves the circle into the room to initiate the game.

In one game, the player controls a pair of scissors, and spiders rapidly descend from the ceiling to the floor on a thread. The player must position the scissors so they can cut the spiders' thread, or the spiders themselves, causing the spider to crash to the floor. If the spider reaches the floor unharmed, the player loses a life. Each round, more spiders descend from the ceiling. Lose 3 lives, and the minigame is lost.

In the next minigame, the player controls a large boot, while ants approach from the two sides of the screen trying to reach the sugar cube in the center of the screen. The player's goal is to stomp the ants to prevent them from reaching the sugar. If the player stomps on the sugar, or the ants reach the sugar, the player loses a life. Lose 3 lives, and the mini-game is over.

In the final mini-game, the player controls a can of bug spray, and must shoot insects as they fly across the screen. If the player contacts the insect, or the insect manages to fly across the screen, the player loses a life. Once again, there's three lives in total.

421861.overview:
Bez-MX is a 1-player versus computer or 2-player competitive wargame.

Two virtually identical countries share a common border. A Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty has kept the peace for many years between these countries, but one stipulation to this deal is forbidding any transportation of weaponry across the border. A minor electronic malfunction in one highly sophisticated BEZ-1 Bomber has caused a simple training mission to turn into war.

There are 3 gameplay options: Basic war, Advanced war, and Solitaire. The player can play versus a computer opponent of varying difficulty, or two player can compete against each other. Players take turns moving their troops and defenses to different locations to avoid enemy fire, as well as launching intercontinental ballistic missiles and bombers at their enemy to attempt to destroy their forces. Players are blinded to their opponents movements on each turn. The game ends when one opponent is entirely destroyed.

424013.overview:
An extremely hard to find game. It is a fantasy adventure where you can create your own characters, choose from a wide inventory of weapons and armor, and use freeform input combined with making choices to explore a dungeon. Watch out for the Chromatic Dragon!

This is a dungeon crawl game - equip your character, enter the dungeon, fight monsters and win treasure; traps abound as well. Many events are random. You can save your character (assuming he survives) to use in later episodes.

Balrog was a 'sampler' of the Maces and Magic series, with only the later ones being full games.

424081.overview:
A diskette compilation of earlier MUSE Software releases, previously only avilable on tape, including four game titles (and one non-game program):

* Tank War
* Maze Game
* Escape!
* Music Box

The six Side Show games (Apple Tree, Minelayer, Pip Shoot, Safecracker, Blockade and Quadripong)

424085.overview:
The Body Transparent is a medical learning game for one or two players.

Designed to teach the major organ systems and the function and diseases thereof, there are two methods of gameplay:* Body Assembly: the player must construct the skeletal system or the major organs or the male or female anatomy by placing the organs on an outline of the human body. Gameplay can occur with or without organ outlines, and the player is rewarded a score based upon how quickly they match pieces.

Body Facts & Functions: the player must match the name, function, major organ system, or related diseases to the correct part of a picture of the human anatomy. The player is rewarded a score based upon how quickly they match pieces.

448933.overview:
Includes the following games:

Bill Budge's Trilogy of Games (1980, Bill Budge/California Pacific Computer) - Includes four games: Night Driver, Pinball, and Space War.

Tranquility Base (1979, Bill Budge) - Clone of Lunar Lander.

Space Album (1980, Bill Budge/California Pacific Computer) - Includes four games: Death Star, Tail Gunner, Asterik, and Solar Shootout.

448957.overview:
A collection of seven games to exercise your brain:-

1) Nuclear Reaction
2) Dodgem
3) Dueling Digits
4) Parrot
5) Midpoints
6) Lines
7) Tones

448976.overview: An action puzzle game, this was preceeded by the game FLoppy, the action is very much in the spirit of BoulderDash but possibly preceeding it. Move around the maze, move and drop the rocks to get to the gems and avoid the various monsters.

455005.overview:
Berserker Raids is a 1 - 2 player science-fiction themed strategy game for multiple systems

From time before human memory, great automated war machines were created by an unknown alien race. These Berserkers, programmed to eliminate all life that they encounter, still roam the galaxy.

Gameplay occurs in a 10 system star cluster. Each player has a home base, and can send out merchant ships to establish production bases in other systems. The player's goal is to strengthen defenses and construct a fleet of their own vessels to counter the Berserker threat. The player can create customized ships that will take a varying number of resources to produce or choose from 5 predefined vessels. The player can possess a maximum fleet of 10 vessels. Each base has a technology and productivity statistic. Technology defines how advanced of ship a base can build, while productivity determines how fast it can build. Each base also has a defensive rating to determine their strength against Berserker attack.

At a varying interval, the Berserker fleet will appear, and begin to hunt for your home base. The bases's missiles will weaken the fleet, and then the player must enter into ship-to-ship combat, which is a strategy affair where ships takes turns attacking and defending. Only 3 ships can engage at one time. Victory is obtained by defeating all of the Berserker vessels, and repossessing all of your original bases.

The game comes preloaded with 10 scenarios, and a corresponding vignette is available in the manual. The player can also create their own novel scenarios.,

455807.overview:
The Breckenridge Caper of 1798 is a text adventure game for the Apple II.

The year is 1798, and given Napoleon Bonaparte's recent victory over British forces at Giza, Egypt, the British government has made every effort possible to obtain knowledge of Napoleon's future plans. Acting in capacity of Ezekiel Breckenridge, an intelligence officer for the British High Command, you have been given explicit orders to patrol a city block in the southern section of Portsmouth. Your mission is to obtain secret documents from a diplomat who's arriving from Calais, France.

456658.overview:
The Brain Machine is a board game construction kit for the Apple II.

Designed to let players create their own custom board games, the player can define the rules and pieces to their choosing. All games occur on a 6 x 6 grid. The player can choose to play against a human opponent, or one of three predefined computer opponents: Cerbrius, Herniak, or Maniac. The package comes with 4 starting games: Check It, Feudal War, Hunter, and jump Over. The player can define the looks of the individual pieces, the starting position of the pieces, how they move, which squares have special characteristics, and how the computer opponents react to different challenges. Board games can be saved to disk, and shared with other players.

456686.overview:
Bezwars is a 2-player competitive arcade game for the Apple II.

A Space Invaders clone where two players directly compete against each other. There are two player-controlled spaceships, one on the top and bottom of the screen facing each other. The ships can move horizontally, and can fire towards the opposing player. In between, a number of alien ships and vessels fire toward the two opponents. The players' goal is to try to destroy their opponent, or have them destroyed by alien fire. If a ship is struck by alien fire, it is destroyed. Each player has 4 spaceships, and the first person to

456689.overview:
Bezman is a 1-player arcade game for the Apple II.

The player controls the titular Bez, as he tries to chomp all of the dots in a maze without coming in contact with the monsters that move randomly about. If the player contacts a monster, they lose a life. When the player chomps all dots, they progress to the next level. They will intermittently encounter special hidden dots which make enemies vulnerable for a short period of time. There are orange doors which allow the player to travel quickly from one side of the maze to the other, and can't be used by enemies. An additional monster is added to the maze every even-numbered level. A new maze design is available every odd-numbered level. The player has a total of 3 lives, and when all are lost, it's game over.

457075.overview:
Backgammon & Checkers is a compilation of two board games for the Apple II. They were released previously already, but not standalone.

Both games are played via text commands. Checkers follows standard rules, and the player must type the coordinates of the piece they wish to move, and where they wish to move it. The goal is to eliminate all of the computer's pieces. Backgammon is a graphical representation of the game board, and once again all commands are via text entry.

460264.overview: Designed for the beginning to intermediate adult Bridge player. Covers basic rules and strategies and explains terminology.

460352.overview:
Bike Hike is an educational memory game for children.

The player goes on a bike ride, and as they peddle about in the park they see a number of items, including: trash bins, rabbits, frogs, deer, flowers, and more. After the bike ride, the player must remember which items they saw, how many, and they are graded on the quality of their memory. The player can choose short or long bike rides, and the number of items progressively increases as the game continues.

460450.overview:
Dragon Side II: The Twisted Speare is a series of 10 add-on scenarios for the text-based RPG Bronze Dragon: Conquest of Infinity.

All commands are via menu structures. From the main menu, the player can create a character, gather a party or construct a castle, or start and adventure.

Characters can be Human, Elf, Dwarf, or Halfling. There are 5 classes: Knight, Assassin, ninja, Elder, and Wizard. Players have limited hit points, bronze pieces, and statistics of Strength, Agility, Intelligence, Constitution, and Endurance.

There are 10 new scenarios, and the player must create a castle for the scenario where they define the number of number of levels and rooms. All scenarios start at the Twisted Speare tavern, where the player can speak with the important characters and receive their upcoming quest. To restock supplies, they must return to the Dragon Village in the main game.

In combat, each player and enemy take turns attacking, advancing, retreating, searching, using inventory items, changing equipment, or fleeing from combat. The player can search for traps, secret passageways, or search enemy corpses while in combat. The player must be within appropriate range to strike an enemy, and their are ranged and close combat weapons. For each attack, the player rolls a number that must be above the enemy's defense to score a hit. There are weapon and agility bonuses for each attack.

464124.overview:
Blisterball! & Mad Bomber! are a series of two 1 or 2-player arcade games for the Apple II.

Both games allow for single-player, as well as 2-player cooperative gameplay. Also allows for 2-player competitive play, where 2 players compete for a high score. The player controls a small ship or cannon on the bottom of the screen, which can move horizontally left and right using the Apple game paddles. The ship fires vertically upwards.

In Blisterball!, the goal is to shoot down bouncing balls as they bounce out of the chamber above the player. If the player is hit by a ball, they are damaged, and they fall into the drain below if they are struck 3 times. There is also a series of blister balls, which can be shot for bonus points.

In Mad Bomber!, the player must shoot bombs as they descend from slots above. If a bomb strikes the bottom of the screen, the player loses a point. 10 points lost, and it's game over. The player must regularly refill their ammo by bringing their ship to the edge of the screen, and if the player is caught in the explosion of a bomb, they lose 10 ammo.

471479.overview: The player controls a large purple boa constrictor, which attempts to hunt mice in a twisty maze. Each level starts with two mice, and if they sneak up behind the player, they will begin to nibble off his tail, leaving the snake shorter. If the mice reach the head, it's game over. If the mice run through the center portion of the level, they will become larger, but can still be eaten. On each level there is a bonus counter that ticks steadily lower, and the player received bonus points if they rapidly eat all the mice. In each level, there are green creatures which randomly appear, and can temporarily block either the snake or the mouse. After eating both mice, the player enters a new stage with a different maze and faster moving mice.

481633.overview:
Compilation of 4 Board Games.

1. Chess

2. Flip-It

3. Connection Plus

4. Trap
